limitations_and_boundaries: scGen has been trained on relatively small datasets that only reflect subsets of biological and transcriptional variability; a trained model cannot be expected to be predictive beyond the domain of the training data.
Predictions require realistic error estimates by holding out parts of the data with known ground truth.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Can a generative model combining variational autoencoders and latent space vector arithmetics accurately predict single-cell perturbation responses out-of-sample?

provenance.text_excerpt: scGen is able to capture both types of responses after stimulation by IFN-β when any of the cell types in the data is held out during training and subsequently predicted

claims.statement: scGen captures cell-type-specific and species-specific responses, including identifying non-responding cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: scGen accurately models perturbation and infection response of cells across cell types, studies and species.

claims.statement: scGen accurately predicts single-cell perturbation response out-of-sample across cell types, studies, and species.

evidence_spans.content: scGen outperforms linear methods, conditional VAEs, and style transfer GANs in out-of-sample prediction of perturbation response.

provenance.text_excerpt: In a broad benchmark, it outperforms other potential modeling approaches, such as linear methods, conditional variational autoencoders (CVAE) and style transfer GANs.

experiments_or_tasks: Cross-study prediction: translate IFN-β effect from study A (Kang et al.) to study B (Zheng et al.).
Predict IFN-β response for all seven cell types in Kang et al. data.
Predict IFN-β-stimulated CD4-T cells from PBMCs (Kang et al.) held out during training.
Predict infection response of intestinal epithelial cells to Salmonella and H. poly (Haber et al.).
Predict LPS response across species (mouse, pig, rabbit, rat) (Hagai et al.).

methods.name: scGen
methods.protocol_description: scGen combines a variational autoencoder (VAE) with latent space vector arithmetics. The VAE encoder maps gene expression to a latent space; the decoder reconstructs expression. Perturbation response is modeled by adding a delta vector (mean difference between perturbed and control latent representations) to the latent representation of a control cell, then decoding. Architecture adapted for scRNA-seq.
